prompts:
Use case: precise-object-edit / style-preserving redesign.
Input image 1 is the approved illustration style and palette reference from the existing HEBUT card set. Transform this into a NEW original shared CARD BACK design; do not make another full-size planet front illustration.

READ THE ORIGINAL BRIEF CAREFULLY: nostalgic 2009–2013 Qzone casual browser game collectible-card aesthetics, especially the friendly, charming, exquisitely illustrated feeling of early 《魔法卡片》. This means a clean 2D Flash-era hand-painted game asset, smooth soft gradients, clearly drawn simplified shapes, a little painterly detail, and delicate small highlights. Cheerful and dreamy for students/adults; not childish preschool, not corporate, not dark ceremonial fantasy. Do not reproduce an official game's actual card frame, logo or asset.

Design a text-free 2:3 portrait card-back INTERIOR, full bleed with NO external border. The core visual should look like an illustrated collectible-card emblem, compact and composed, not a space poster.
Color: medium soft sky blue at outer areas, pale cornflower and soft lilac in the inner field, cream yellow and warm ivory accents. Navy only in fine outlines and small supporting details. An airy luminous pastel overall impression. Smooth clean cartoon gradients with minimal grain, NOT rough watercolor/canvas/noisy oil texture.

Composition:
- A simple original rounded cartouche centered in the canvas, about 70% of the width, beginning around 25% and ending around 75% of canvas height.
- Its upper portion contains ONE appealing pale-cream-and-soft-blue ringed planet, a small graceful four-point golden star beside it, and soft rounded cloud curls tucked around its base. The planet is a neatly drawn cartoon celestial object with two or three broad smooth color bands, subtle blue outline and gentle highlight. No eyes or face. Keep the ring structurally coherent: back part behind globe, front part crossing in front. This should feel like a prized collectible motif, not a realistic Saturn image or plastic toy.
- Beneath the planet, integrate a softly raised ivory/cream blank rounded ribbon/plaque into the cloud-scroll cartouche. This plaque must provide a clean wide undivided central surface for TWO short lines of editable typography to be added later. Place the blank face approximately x=20%..80%, y=58%..72%, wide enough for a Chinese series title. Hint at folded ribbon ends on each side with simple sky-blue outlines. No tiny compartment boxes, no lettering.
- Let the vignette breathe: plenty of clear sky above and below it. Only a FEW small stars and a single subtle trailing arc around the central motif, not concentric magic circles. Around the edges include sparse very low contrast tiny planet/star silhouette motifs, like a tasteful old browser-game collectible card pattern, about 8 motifs TOTAL. Low visual weight, not a wallpaper full of dots.
- A few small rounded cloud curls at top-left and bottom-right corners complement the central vignette. They must be flat hand-drawn game ornament shapes with clean curves, not realistic billowing clouds, ribbons of smoke or thick brushstrokes.
- Preserve a simple readable silhouette at thumbnail size.

Must avoid the rejected version: NO dark blue night sky, NO giant golden compass/star in a huge circular astrolabe, NO thin complicated orbital diagram, NO metal heraldic shield, NO gold filigree luxury certificate, NO dense stars, NO nebula realism, NO modern minimal corporate layout. No dramatic glow, no neon, no mechanical sci-fi HUD, no photorealistic 3D, no clay/figurine/blind-box look, no baby faces. NO text, NO letters, NO number, NO logo, NO watermark. Keep all text editable and outside this bitmap layer. Produce one finished illustration, portrait 2:3.
